title: A chosen finite algebra generating family and its differentials after scalar extension
statement: Let $A_0,B_0,C_0,T$ be commutative rings, let $B_0,C_0,T$ be $A_0$-algebras, and let $\varphi_0:B_0\to C_0$ be an $A_0$-algebra map. Fix $m\ge0$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_m\in C_0$ such that every element of $C_0$ is a polynomial in the $x_r$ with coefficients in $B_0$ (acting through $\varphi_0$). Put $B_T=T\otimes_{A_0}B_0$, $C_T=T\otimes_{A_0}C_0$, with $B_T\to C_T$ given by $t\otimes b\mapsto t\otimes\varphi_0(b)$, and put $x_{r,T}=1\otimes x_r$. Tensor products use [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with the ring multiplication $(t\otimes c)(u\otimes c')=tu\otimes cc'$. Then the $x_{r,T}$ generate $C_T$ as a $B_T$-algebra. More explicitly, if $c=\sum_e\varphi_0(b_e)\prod_r x_r^{e_r}$ is any finite polynomial expression, then $t\otimes c=\sum_e(t\otimes b_e)\prod_r x_{r,T}^{e_r}$ in $C_T$, where coefficients from $B_T$ act via the displayed map. For the universal differentials of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], the family $(\mathrm d x_r)_r$ spans $\Omega_{C_0/B_0}$ as a $C_0$-module and $(\mathrm d x_{r,T})_r$ spans $\Omega_{C_T/B_T}$ as a $C_T$-module. For $y_r=x_r$ over $B_0$, or $y_r=x_{r,T}$ over $B_T$, any coefficient $b$ in the respective base and any $e\in\mathbf N^m$ satisfy $\mathrm d(b\prod_r y_r^{e_r})=\sum_{r:e_r>0}e_r b\prod_{s\ne r}y_s^{e_s}y_r^{e_r-1}\,\mathrm d y_r$, and this formula extends additively to polynomial expressions. The empty family $m=0$ is allowed; both differential modules are then zero.

proof.text: For each exponent vector $e$, the stated tensor-ring multiplication gives $\prod_r(1\otimes x_r)^{e_r}=1\otimes\prod_r x_r^{e_r}$: start with the empty product $1\otimes1$ and multiply by one factor $1\otimes x_r$ at a time. Multiplying by the image of $t\otimes b$ gives $t\otimes(\varphi_0(b)\prod_r x_r^{e_r})$. Bilinearity in the second variable then gives exactly the asserted formula for $t\otimes c$ for any chosen finite expression for $c$.

proof.text: Every element of $C_T$ is a finite sum of pure tensors: the tensor-definition node says these generate as an $A_0$-module, and a scalar $a$ is absorbed by $a(t\otimes c)=(at)\otimes c$. Choose a polynomial expression for the second factor of each pure tensor and apply step 1. The resulting finite sum is a polynomial in the $x_{r,T}$ with coefficients in $B_T$, proving generation. No flatness or injectivity of any ring map is used.

proof.text: Work in either pair $(R,S,y)=(B_0,C_0,x)$ or $(B_T,C_T,x_T)$, and let $\mathrm d$ denote its universal derivation. The differential-definition node gives additivity, Leibniz, and $\mathrm d b=0$ for a coefficient from $R$. Thus $\mathrm d1=0$ and $\mathrm d(bz)=b\,\mathrm dz$. Induction on $n\geq1$ gives $\mathrm d(z^n)=n z^{n-1}\mathrm dz$: the case $n=1$ is the identity, and Leibniz applied to $z^nz$ changes the coefficient $n$ to $n+1$. For $n=0$ the derivative is zero.

source.place: Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), first proof paragraph, Leibniz induction; Tag 07BK (definition-differentials), preceding quotient construction, and Tag 00RO (lemma-universal-omega).

proof.text: Apply Leibniz successively to the finite product $\prod_r y_r^{e_r}$. More explicitly, the product of zero factors has derivative zero; appending a factor $z$ to a product $u$ gives $u\,\mathrm dz+z\,\mathrm du$, so induction gives one summand for each factor. Insert the power formula of step 3, omit the factors with exponent zero, and multiply by $b$ using $\mathrm d(bz)=b\,\mathrm dz$. This gives the displayed monomial formula with only nonnegative exponents. Additivity gives the formula for any finite polynomial sum.

source.place: Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), first proof paragraph, Leibniz induction; Tag 07BK (definition-differentials), preceding quotient construction, and Tag 00RO (lemma-universal-omega).

proof.text: The quotient construction in the differential-definition node shows that every element of $\Omega_{S/R}$ is a finite $S$-linear combination of classes $\mathrm ds$. Each $s$ is a polynomial in $y$ (the hypothesis for $C_0$, step 2 for $C_T$); step 4 expresses $\mathrm ds$ as a linear combination of the $\mathrm dy_r$. Substitution proves both spanning assertions. If $m=0$, each polynomial is a coefficient, so every $\mathrm ds$ is zero and both modules are zero; the monomial sum is empty as required.

lean.statement: theorem baseChanged_algebra_differential_generators {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {C : Type w} {T : Type z} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C] [CommRing T] [Algebra A B] [Algebra A C] [Algebra A T] (φ : B →ₐ[A] C) (m : ℕ) (x : Fin m → C) (hx : Function.Surjective (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom φ.toRingHom x)) : Function.Surjective (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom (TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id A T) φ).toRingHom (fun r ↦ (1 : T) ⊗ₜ[A] x r)) ∧ (∀ (t : T) (c : C) (s : Finset (Fin m → ℕ)) (b : (Fin m → ℕ) → B), c = ∑ e ∈ s, φ (b e) * ∏ r, x r ^ e r → t ⊗ₜ[A] c = ∑ e ∈ s, TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id A T) φ (t ⊗ₜ[A] b e) * ∏ r, ((1 : T) ⊗ₜ[A] x r) ^ e r) ∧ KaehlerDifferential.ChosenGeneratorFormulas φ.toRingHom x ∧ KaehlerDifferential.ChosenGeneratorFormulas (TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id A T) φ).toRingHom (fun r ↦ (1 : T) ⊗ₜ[A] x r)
